newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BolsWessanen profits plunge, sees better 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: BolsWessanen profits plunge, sees better 2nd half.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen NV reported first-half profits down by 22 percent on Wednesday, but said it expected to halve the profit fall over the full year.

The group posted first-half net profits from ordinary operations of 68.9 million guilders ($41.6 million) -- up slightly on most analysts' forecasts -- compared with 87.9 million guilders in the year-earlier period.

"Based on the outlook for the remainder of the year, the earlier announced expectation is maintained that net income from ordinary activities over full 1996 will decrease by about 10 percent," it said in a statement.
But it warned that further restructuring would result in additional extraordinary charges in the second half totalling between 10 and 15 million guilders.
The news gained a cool reception on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, where BolsWessanen shares shed 0.90 guilders to close at 27.50 after trading up 0.30 guilders previously.

"The fact that BolsWessanen hasn't further downgraded its forecast is positive, but I think that it will have some trouble meeting its target," ING Barings analyst Gerard Rijk said in an initial reaction ahead of a briefing on Thursday.
"I think investors will have been disappointed by news of yet more extraordinary charges," he added.
A 5.4 million guilder book loss on the sale of BolsWessanen's German drinks maker Strothmann earlier this year shaved total first-half net to 63.5 million.
The company said profits had been hurt by deteriorating results of its cereals business, lower exports of spirits and falling margins on its U.S. dairy activities.
Chairman Mac Zondervan told a news conference profits were down largely due to incidental factors.
"Dairy U.S was hit by extremely sharp butter fat price increases...while cereals (grouped under 'other consumer products') were down sharply due mainly to restructuring in the U.K.," he said.
Butter fat prices jumped by an average of six to 15 percent per month in the latter part of the first half.
"These exceptional market circumstances are not expected to be repeated," Zondervan said.
Operating income for dairy as a whole fell some 17 percent to 39.5 million guilders.
Lower margins on cereals helped pull down operating income from other consumer products by 29 percent to 35.6 million.

Here too the fall was largely incidental, Zondervan said, with around a third to one half of the profit fall in cereals accounted for by temporarily higher costs of production and distribution due to restructuring in the U.K.

In 1995, BolsWessanen posted a full-year net profit from ordinary operations of 202.9 million guilders, down from 254.1 million in the previous year. The total 1995 net after one-off items was 205.8 million compared with 254.1 million in 1994. ($ = 1.658 Dutch Guilders)
